glossary.hyperlipidaemia: Raised levels of fats such as cholesterol in the blood.
glossary.unilateral: Affecting one side of the body only.
glossary.facial droop: Sagging of one side of the face from weakness of the facial muscles.
glossary.numbness: Loss or reduction of sensation in part of the body.
glossary.PCA: Posterior cerebral artery, which supplies the occipital lobe and visual cortex.
glossary.posterior cerebral artery: Artery supplying the back of the brain, including the visual cortex.
glossary.optic chiasm: Point behind the eyes where fibres from the inner half of each retina cross over.
glossary.occipital cortex: Back part of the brain that processes vision.
glossary.ischaemic stroke: Death of brain tissue caused by a blocked artery.
glossary.completed stroke: A stroke whose symptoms have not resolved, meaning brain infarction has occurred.
glossary.stroke: Sudden loss of brain function from blocked or burst blood vessels lasting over 24 hours or with infarction.
glossary.hypoglycaemia: Low blood glucose, which can mimic stroke or TIA with focal symptoms.
glossary.capillary glucose: Finger-prick blood glucose measured at the bedside.
glossary.ECG: Electrocardiogram, a recording of the heart's electrical activity; used here to look for AF.
glossary.MRI: Magnetic resonance imaging, a detailed scan using magnets rather than radiation.
glossary.CT: Computed tomography, a cross-sectional X-ray scan.
glossary.non-contrast CT: CT scan without injected dye, best for quickly spotting fresh bleeding in the brain.
glossary.haemorrhage: Bleeding; here bleeding into or around the brain.
glossary.warfarin: Oral anticoagulant that blocks vitamin K-dependent clotting factors; needs INR monitoring.
glossary.anticoagulation: Treatment that reduces the blood's ability to clot.
glossary.anticoagulated: Taking a drug that reduces blood clotting, such as warfarin or a DOAC.
glossary.bleeding disorder: Condition such as haemophilia where the blood does not clot normally.
glossary.aspirin: Antiplatelet drug that irreversibly blocks COX, reducing platelet clumping.
glossary.contraindicated: Should not be given because it could cause harm in this patient.
glossary.secondary prevention: Treatment to stop a further event in someone who has already had one.
glossary.high-intensity statin: Statin dose that lowers LDL cholesterol by 40% or more, such as atorvastatin 80 mg.
glossary.statin: Cholesterol-lowering drug that blocks HMG-CoA reductase in the liver.
glossary.antiplatelet: Drug that stops platelets sticking together to form clots.
glossary.endarterectomy: Surgery to open an artery and remove the plaque lining it.
glossary.contralateral: On the opposite side; the carotid lesion is opposite the weak side of the body.
glossary.thrombus: Blood clot formed inside a vessel.
glossary.embolic: Caused by material (usually clot) travelling in the blood and lodging downstream.
glossary.thrombotic: Caused by a clot forming at the site of blockage.
glossary.atherosclerotic plaque: Fatty, fibrous deposit in an artery wall that narrows it and can rupture.
glossary.carotid atherosclerosis: Fatty plaque build-up in the carotid arteries in the neck.
glossary.embolises: Breaks off and travels in the bloodstream to block a smaller vessel.
glossary.distally: Further along the vessel, away from the heart.
glossary.GI bleeding: Bleeding from anywhere in the gut, a key risk with aspirin.
glossary.NICE: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence, which writes UK treatment guidelines.
glossary.neurological dysfunction: Abnormal function of the brain, spinal cord or nerves.
glossary.crescendo: Increasingly frequent episodes in a short time, signalling high stroke risk.
glossary.hemianopia: Loss of vision in half of the visual field.
glossary.DAPT: Dual antiplatelet therapy, two antiplatelet drugs such as aspirin plus clopidogrel.
